- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 5–10% in early/medium horizon.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; apply downward bias of 5–15% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model may lag in adjusting; anticipate mean reversion and reduce forecast by 3–8% for 2–4 days.
- In 30-day horizon, model frequently overestimates early in the forecast window; apply downward correction of 3–7% for first 5–7 days.
- When sentiment history shows alternating +/– patterns, model tends to overfit recent trends; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values before final output.
- If true outcome shows sudden drop after spike, model often fails to recognize it; add 1–3 day lag correction for downward moves.
- For sentiment-heavy negative periods, model underestimates volatility; increase forecast variance by 10–20% for 3–5 day horizon to account for risk.
